_comment: The hook wiring nightshift needs, as a fragment of .claude/settings.json.
`nightshift init` merges this into an existing settings.json rather than
overwriting it: a project's `permissions` block is its own and must survive.
EVERY command here is `python -m nightshift.<module>`, never a repo-relative
path. A relative command is resolved against the SESSION's cwd, so a stray
`cd` in an unrelated Bash call disarms the guard instead of tripping it
enforces that, and `nightshift.hooks.project_script` is the cwd-independent
way to reach a script that must stay project-side.
The PostToolUse dispatcher (`nightshift.hooks.post`) runs the gates and always
exits 0 on purpose: a violation must show in the transcript, not block the edit
that would fix it. It prints only what is news since the previous edit. A project
names its own after-edit scripts as arguments: `nightshift.hooks.post <script>`.
`nightshift.hooks.pre` runs every PreToolUse fence in one process (its `RULES`);
one spawn per tool call instead of one per fence.
`nightshift.hooks.commit_pathspec` reads what that run last recorded and refuses
a commit while it is red, in addition to its pathspec check -- so the gap between
a red gate result shown once and the next `git push` (which is as far as
`preflight_guard` reaches) is closed at commit time instead.
